item.title: Houston Rockets Free Agency: The Surprising Moves Reshaping 2026
item.description:
The Houston Rockets entered the 2026 offseason with championship expectations still stinging from a first-round playoff exit. Now they are moving fast — and not in the direction most fans predicted.

Instead of chasing a splashy shooting star, Houston opened free agency by signing a defensive veteran guard. Then they added a proven marksman. The message is clear: the Rockets are retooling, not rebuilding.

Quick Summary: The Houston Rockets agreed to a deal with veteran guard Marcus Smart, added shooting help in Bogdan Bogdanovic, and kept Fred VanVleet after he exercised his $25 million player option. The surprising Houston Rockets free agency strategy is built on defense, depth, and a Kevin Durant–led core.

item.title: Marcus Smart's Stunning Lakers Revival Rewrites 2026 Playoffs
item.description:
Nine games in street clothes. Nine games of doubt. Then Marcus Smart walked into Game 2 and shredded the Houston Rockets for 25 points, five threes, seven assists, and five steals.

If you thought the Lakers’ 2026 playoff run would hinge on LeBron James and Deandre Ayton alone, Smart just changed your mind.

Quick Summary: Marcus Smart signed a two-year, $11 million deal with the Lakers in July 2025. After battling injuries that cost him nine late-season games, he erupted in Game 2 of the first round, leading Los Angeles to a 101-94 win and a 2-0 series lead over Houston.
